key_insight: InterPrior introduces a scalable, physics-aware generative prior that lets high-level intentions (e.g., affordances) drive physically coherent whole-body human–object interactions without hand-designing low-level motion plans. By scaling this prior, coordinated balance, contact, and manipulation emerge naturally from the model rather than from explicit per-task controllers.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-level intent and low-level, physically consistent whole-body loco-manipulation by removing the need to plan explicit joint-level movements for every interaction and enabling generalization across objects and contexts.
method: Learn a large-scale generative prior over human–object interaction dynamics that captures contact, balance, and manipulation patterns from simulated and/or recorded interaction data.

Use a hierarchical control pipeline: condition the prior on high-level affordance/intention and sample candidate motions, then enforce physics-aware constraints (contact consistency, balance, object dynamics) to produce executable whole-body trajectories.
Design the system for scalability and compositionality so the learned prior generalizes across diverse objects, tasks, and environments, enabling reuse of motor primitives for novel interactions.
impact: Enables practitioners to build controllers and simulators that convert simple intent signals into realistic, physically plausible whole-body interactions—reducing manual engineering and improving generalization for robotics, animation, and embodied AI.

paper_title: InterPrior: Scaling Generative Control for Physics-Based Human-Object Interactions
paper_authors: Sirui Xu, Samuel Schulter, Morteza Ziyadi, Xialin He, Xiaohan Fei
